Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: What position does Valentine Ayika currently or formerly hold?
Document 1: Title: The Unwavering Voice of the People: The Story of Valentine Ayika

In the heart of Nigeria, where the rhythms of democracy pulsed through the veins of its citizens, a stalwart leader emerged to champion the cause of the people. Valentine Ayika, a seasoned politician, stood tall as a beacon of hope, his name etched in the annals of Nigerian politics as a member of the House of Representatives of Nigeria. The year was 2015, and the political landscape of Nigeria was abuzz with anticipation. The general elections were around the corner, and the people were eager to exercise their right to choose their leaders. Amidst the sea of aspirants, Valentine Ayika's name resonated with the masses, his reputation as a champion of the common man preceding him. As the election results rolled in, it became clear that Ayika's message of hope and change had struck a chord with the electorate. He emerged victorious, his name etched on the ballot as the winner of the federal constituency seat. The people had spoken, and their voice was loud and clear: Valentine Ayika was their chosen representative in the hallowed halls of the House of Representatives. Ayika's journey to the House of Representatives was not a chance occurrence. It was the culmination of years of dedicated service to his community, his state, and his nation. A seasoned politician with a deep understanding of the intricacies of governance, he had cut his teeth in the rough-and-tumble world of Nigerian politics, earning the respect and admiration of his peers and constituents alike. As a member of the House of Representatives, Ayika was a vocal advocate for the rights of the marginalized and the oppressed. He championed causes that resonated with the common man, from education and healthcare to infrastructure development and economic empowerment. His was a voice that echoed through the chambers of the National Assembly, a clarion call to action that inspired his colleagues to work towards a better Nigeria. The evidence of Ayika's membership in the House of Representatives is not limited to his electoral victory. It is reflected in the numerous bills he sponsored, the motions he moved, and the debates he participated in. His contributions to the legislative process were marked by a deep sense of purpose and a commitment to the welfare of his constituents. One such instance was his spirited defense of the 2016 budget, which he argued was critical to the development of Nigeria's infrastructure.
Document 2: As the sun set over the Amsterdam canals, casting a warm orange glow over the city, Valentine Ayika made her way to the Binnenhof, the historic heart of Dutch politics. She had grown accustomed to the grandeur of the building, but still felt a flutter in her chest every time she walked through its ornate doors. It was a reminder that she, a Nigerian-born politician, had earned a seat at the table in this esteemed institution. Valentine's assistant, a bright and ambitious young woman named Sophie, greeted her with a warm smile and a folder full of briefing papers. "Good morning, Ms. Ayika. Today's agenda is packed, but I've highlighted the key points for you." Valentine nodded her thanks, her eyes scanning the documents as she made her way to the chamber. As she took her seat among the other members of the House of Representatives, Valentine felt a sense of pride and responsibility wash over her. It was a feeling she had grown familiar with over the past three years, since her election to the Tweede Kamer, the Dutch parliament's lower house. Her colleagues, a diverse group of individuals from all corners of the Netherlands, nodded in greeting as she settled in for the day's debates. The first item on the agenda was a discussion on climate change, and Valentine was prepared to make her voice heard. She had spent countless hours researching the issue, meeting with experts and constituents alike, and was determined to push for meaningful action. As she stood to address the chamber, her words were met with nods of agreement and murmurs of approval from her fellow representatives. It was moments like these that Valentine felt most at home in her adopted country. She had left Nigeria as a young woman, seeking new opportunities and a fresh start. The Netherlands had welcomed her with open arms, and she had worked tirelessly to make a difference in her new community. Now, as a member of the House of Representatives, she was proud to be a part of the country's decision-making process. As the day drew to a close, Valentine gathered her things and made her way back to her office. Sophie was waiting for her, a cup of steaming coffee in hand. "You did great today, Ms. Ayika," she said, with a smile. Valentine smiled back, feeling a sense of satisfaction wash over her.
